lead: the stair, the roof timbers, the benches in the hall on that road: all of it left your hands, and forty years on there is still nothing in that village that needs your attention.
sun: your hands go, without ever being directed there, to the part of a place that takes weight: the tread that has never given, the frame carrying a roof through forty winters, the bench four people lean their whole working day on. all of it sits in plain view. all of it stopped being an object about a month after you fitted it and became the room, which is what a thing does when it works.
moon: the making itself keeps no ledger, and never has. a thing gets needed on a tuesday and exists by the weekend, at your own expense, with no figure attached and no note of where it went. so the count of what you have put into that road was never taken, by you or by anybody, and the road could not produce one now if it tried.
pull: every piece of it is still carrying and none of it is an object any more — a whole working life turned into the ordinary condition of one road.
tension: your kitchen has a door that has not closed properly since your mother died, a joke in that family for nine years. the ones telling it are not being cruel. somebody who reframed their entire upstairs in a weekend and will not spend an hour on a hinge of their own looks like modesty, or stubbornness, and neither is in it. what pulls your hands is weight wanting to be carried, and a door that sticks is carrying fine.
cost: a thing that was wrong on wednesday is right by friday, at no charge, with no meeting about it, and it holds for four decades. nothing you made has ever needed a second visit. a second visit is the only event that puts anybody in front of the work wondering who made it, so that road has had forty years of your hands and no occasion to consider them.

lead: there is a plaque on it with your name spelled correctly, and the building has been photographed for the county's own publicity, and in eleven years nobody who uses it every week has thought about it once.
sun: what you put up was a boundary before it was anything else: an inside and an outside, weight taken and passed down. it went up correctly and has not moved since. a structure that does not move hands the people using it nothing to hold an opinion about — they have opinions about the parking, because the parking changes. the building has been the plain condition of a saturday there ever since.
moon: the admiration is genuine and all of it stands at a distance. four other counties have the same solution now, two of them working from drawings you sent. none of that has been raised by you with anyone. putting a condition on the drawings did not present itself as a task then and does not now. what the town reads in is unowned in every sense but the metal.
pull: your name is on it, at eye height, in a font chosen by a committee, and the people it keeps dry have never read it, and the ones who copied it did not need to.
tension: the trade's read is that you did nicely out of one good idea; the read at home is that you never made anything of it; both are looking at the same object. what would settle either is a sentence about what it took, and that sentence has never formed in you, any more than the instinct to guard the drawings did. so the plaque does all of your arguing, and a plaque cannot answer a stranger who has already decided.
cost: eleven years of use, and it has not closed for a single day, which is why four other places wanted the design and why yours is simply where the town goes on a saturday. the exposure and the invisibility arrived together and are one condition. you are entirely locatable and nothing has ever been asked of you, since the thing they admire is finished, standing, and asks after nobody.

lead: ask any four of them what you do at the trust and you get four answers, all partial, all fond. the terms they signed on their first day were written by you, and nobody has read past page two.
sun: the actual work is the edge — which cases the trust takes and which it refuses, what happens to staff in a bad year, where the money stops whoever is asking. all of it is on paper, signed, at the desk. none of it is a role. a boundary is not a task performed on a given morning; it holds or it does not, and yours has held through two recessions and one death.
moon: nothing in that fits a title. yours has changed four times in twenty years, each time into something a new chief executive could put on a chart, and each caught a different quarter. you did not manoeuvre toward this and could not have described it in advance. what you are is the outline the place has, and an outline is not one of the things standing inside it.
pull: four job titles, none of them right, and the entire character of a place sits in a document you wrote that nobody has read since the day they signed it.
tension: at parties, and in every new director's first month, the same friendly question arrives: what is it you actually do there. the honest answer runs nine minutes and lands, out loud, as somebody claiming to be the reason a charity works. so the short one gets given instead, which is administration, and it is accepted at once, and the person who accepted it spends a year walking into edges they cannot account for and filing them under culture.
cost: nobody at that trust has had a bad decision arrive from a direction the terms did not cover, in twenty years, and none has needed to know it. a thing that holds is never examined, so none of it has been praised or contested. when you go, no post gets advertised, the place carries on as it is, and that will be read as evidence it was never you.

lead: two of the four have not spoken in three years, and what they are pulling at is the arrangement you put up around them all, while the eleven on the shop floor think the yard is having an ordinary year.
sun: you are not in this to be right. what you built is the enclosure both are standing in — the terms, the way the money divides, the settlement that survived the thin year — and a structure takes load from both sides or it takes none. your position is structural rather than moral, and neither of them can locate it, because neither has met somebody in a fight who was not trying to win it.
moon: you carry both arguments the way a frame carries a roof: from opposite sides, at once, with neither one made smaller to let the other through. her case about the money is sound. his about how the decision got taken is also sound. reducing either has been available every week for three years and has never looked like the answer, and the two are still in the same building.
pull: three years in a fight you have never wanted either side to lose, and the eleven whose livelihoods are inside it have noticed nothing — a thing under load looks like a thing at rest.
tension: each has told a third party that you are with the other, which is the only reading available when somebody will not produce a verdict. the true sentence — that the arrangement will still be standing when both of them have gone, and is carrying eleven households meanwhile — comes out of a mouth as a person who cares more about a yard than about people you have known for twenty years. neither of them has ever heard it.
cost: no redundancy in three years, no customer lost, the accounts clean, because the structure took the whole weight of it while the two of them fought inside. the weight came through you. neither of them has had cause to learn that, since nothing gave, and a thing that never gives cannot report what went through it.
